what_it_does: The AI industry measures how fast systems are with benchmarks (standardized tests), but until now there was no agreed-upon, reproducible way to measure how much energy those systems consume — making it impossible to compare the energy efficiency of, say, a tiny IoT sensor chip versus a warehouse-scale GPU cluster running the same AI workload. MLPerf Power extends the widely adopted MLPerf benchmark family (a set of standardized AI tests developed by a broad industry coalition) with standardized power measurement rules: how to attach power meters, at what granularity (individual device, server rack, or entire data center), and which workloads to run. The methodology was developed by more than 20 companies and applied to collect 1,841 reproducible energy measurements across 60 different systems, spanning from sub-milliwatt microcontrollers up to megawatt data-center installations, enabling fair apples-to-apples energy-efficiency comparisons across wildly different hardware.
